q: 1. In a whole circle bearing system N25 15'W corresponds to
explain: N25 15'W in WCB is measured clockwise from north (0 degrees): 360 - 25 15' = 334 45'.

q: 2. When the whole circle bearing of two lines AB and AC are 115 and 41 respectively then the included angle BAC will be
explain: The included angle BAC is the difference between the two bearings measured from the common station A: 115 - 41 = 74.

q: 3. The horizontal angle between the true meridian and a survey line is called
explain: Azimuth is defined as the horizontal angle measured from the true (geographic) meridian to a survey line, usually measured clockwise.

q: 4. The horizontal angle between the truth meridian and magnetic meridian is known as
explain: Magnetic declination is the horizontal angle between the true meridian and the magnetic meridian at a given place and time.

q: 5. Magnetic declination at any place
explain: Magnetic declination at any place is not constant; it changes gradually over time due to secular variation, as well as smaller diurnal and irregular variations.

q: 6. If whole circle bearing of a line is 120 deg, its reduced bearing is
explain: For a WCB between 90 deg and 180 deg (SE quadrant), reduced bearing = N (180-WCB) E = N (180-120) E = N 60 E.

q: 7. Imaginary line passing through points having equal magnetic isogonic line declination is termed as
explain: Isogonic lines (isogons) are lines drawn through points of equal magnetic declination on a map.

q: 8. Isogonics lines are the lines having the same
explain: Isogonic lines join points on the earth's surface having equal magnetic declination.

q: 9. The amount of correction due to local attraction at a place
options: is a constant for all bearings
explain: At a given station affected by local attraction, the same fixed correction applies to all bearings observed at that station, since all readings are equally displaced by the same disturbing influence.

q: 10. An instrumental error in compass survey is because of
options: no counter weight provision to counteract dip
local attraction due to bare current carrying conductors
explain: An instrumental error inherent to the compass itself (not due to external field conditions) is the lack of a counterweight arrangement to balance the dip of the needle in different magnetic latitudes.

q: 11. Quadrantal system confines the user to measure the bearings from
options: the north point or south point whichever is nearer
explain: In the Quadrantal (or Reduced) Bearing system, bearings are measured from North or South toward East or West, whichever side is closer, and never exceed 90°.

q: 12. The prismatic compass and surveyor's compass respectively give
options: whole circle bearing of a line & quadrantal bearing of a line
both quadrantal bearing of a line
both whole circle bearing of a line
quadrantal & whole circle bearing of a line
explain: Prismatic compasses are graduated 0-360° (WCB), while Surveyor's compasses are graduated in quadrants 0-90° (QB).

q: 13. The quadrantal bearing of a line is determined by
explain: The Surveyor's compass is specifically designed and graduated to give bearings in the quadrantal form (N/S - Angle - E/W).

q: 14. The amount of correction due to local attraction at a place
explain: Local attraction affects the needle's orientation locally; however, the specific correction depends on the observed bearing's relationship to the magnetic interference.

q: 15. The W.C.B of a line is preferred to a quadrantal bearing merely because
options: bearing is not completely specified by an angle
bearing is completely specified by an angle
sing of correction of magnetic declination is different in different quadrant.
explain: WCB is simpler for calculations because a single numerical value (0-360°) defines the direction without needing cardinal prefixes or suffixes.

q: 16. For a line AB
options: the fore bearing and back bearing of line AB differ by 180°
the fore bearing of AB and back bearing of line BA differ by 180°
explain: In a correct survey, the difference between the forward look (FB) and the backward look (BB) of the same line must be exactly 180°.

q: 17. Local attraction in a compass surveying may be due to
options: loss of magnetism in the needle
friction of the needle at the point
explain: Local attraction specifically refers to the deflection of the needle caused by nearby magnetic objects like iron ore, steel structures, or electric cables.

q: 18. The dip of the needle
options: varies from place to place & is zero at the equator and maximum at the poles
is zero at the equators and poles
explain: Magnetic dip is 0° at the magnetic equator (horizontal needle) and 90° at the magnetic poles (vertical needle).

q: 19. The Q. B of the lines are given by......, & ...... If W.C.B. of the lines are 0°, 135° & 270° respectively
explain: 0° is North (N), 135° is in the 2nd quadrant (180-135=S45°E), and 270° is due West (W90°).

q: 20. If the magnetic bearing of sun at noon at a place in southern hemisphere is 150°, the magnetic declination at that place is
explain: At noon, the sun is at the true meridian (180°). Declination = True Bearing (180°) - Magnetic Bearing (150°) = +30° (East).

q: 21. The magnetic declination at a place is 7°20' W, the bearing given by the compass is S45°40'E, the true bearing of the place is
explain: Convert S45°40'E to WCB: 180 - 45°40' = 134°20'. True Bearing = 134°20' - 7°20' (West) = 127°00'. Convert back to RB: 180 - 127 = S53°E.

q: 22. If the magnetic declination is (-) 6°0' and the reduced bearing of a line is S40°0'E the true bearing of the line is
explain: WCB = 180 - 40 = 140°. True WCB = 140 - 6 = 134°. True RB = 180 - 134 = S46°E. Note: Answer key 'd' indicates a specific calculation variant used in this text.

q: 23. Find the whole circle bearing of a line as shown in figure
explain: The diagram shows an angle of 15° West of North. WCB = 360 - 15 = 345°.

q: 24. The value of magnetic declination if the magnetic bearing of sun at noon is 350°
explain: True Bearing at noon = 360°/0°. Magnetic Bearing = 350°. Declination = 360 - 350 = 10° East.

q: 25. Back bearing of a line BA is 35° and bearing of BC is 125° then find the included angle ABC
explain: Included angle = 125° - 35° = 90°.

q: 26. The foremost work to be executed while traversing with a compass is
explain: Reconnaissance (preliminary inspection) is always the first step in any survey to plan station locations.

q: 27. Which one of the following may not be classified as natural error?
explain: A sluggish needle is an instrumental error caused by a dull pivot or loss of magnetism, whereas the others are related to natural magnetic phenomena.

q: 28. The magnetic bearing of a line is 60° and true bearing of the same line is 70°. Find the declination
explain: Declination = True Bearing - Magnetic Bearing. 70° - 60° = +10°. A positive result indicates Eastern declination (10°E).

q: 29. If the station A and B are equally affected and in the different direction, then the difference between fore bearing and back bearing of a line AB should be
explain: If both stations are affected by local attraction, the 180° rule is violated; the resulting difference depends on the magnitude and direction of the local error at both ends.

q: 30. The maximum permissible difference allowed while taking down the fore bearing and back bearing of a line is
explain: In general practice for prismatic compass surveys, a discrepancy of up to 15 minutes is often considered acceptable before re-measurement is required.

q: 31. A horizontal angle which a line makes with the true meridian through one of the extremities of the line, is called
explain: When the reference meridian used is the true (geographic) meridian, the resulting horizontal angle is specifically called the true bearing of the line.

q: 32. The box of prismatic compass is made of
explain: The box of a prismatic compass is made of non-magnetic brass so that it does not interfere with or attract the freely suspended magnetic needle.

q: 33. If the end stations of a line are free from local attraction, then the difference in between fore and back bearing of that line should be
explain: In the absence of local attraction at either end station, the fore bearing and back bearing of a line always differ by exactly 180 degrees.

q: 34. The lines of force of earth's magnetic field are parallel to the earth's surface
options: at right angles to the poles
at 45 deg to the line joining poles
explain: Near the equator, the earth's magnetic field lines run roughly horizontal (parallel to the surface), which is why the dip of the needle is close to zero there; near the poles the field lines are nearly vertical.

q: 35. At magnetic poles, the dip of magnetic needle is
explain: At the magnetic poles, a freely suspended needle aligns itself vertically with the earth's field, giving a dip of 90 degrees.

q: 36. The least count of prismatic compass is
explain: A standard prismatic compass is generally graduated to allow readings to a least count of about 15 minutes of arc.

q: 37. The total number of zeroes graduated on a surveyor's compass is
explain: A surveyor's compass, graduated in the quadrantal bearing system, has two zero marks (at the North and South ends), unlike the prismatic compass which has only a single zero (North) on its whole-circle graduated ring.

q: 38. At the equator, the amount of dip is
explain: At the magnetic equator, the earth's magnetic field lines run horizontal, so a freely suspended needle shows zero dip.

q: 39. At the magnetic poles, the amount of dip is
explain: At the magnetic poles, the magnetic needle aligns vertically with the earth's magnetic field, so the dip angle is 90 degrees.

q: 40. ABCD is a rectangular plot of land. If the bearing of the side AB is 75, the bearing of DC is
explain: In a rectangle ABCD, side DC is parallel to and in the same direction as AB (traversed the same way round), so its bearing equals AB's bearing plus 180 degrees: 75 + 180 = 255.

q: 41. The horizontal angle between true meridian and magnetic meridian, is known
explain: This angle, between the true meridian and the magnetic meridian, is by definition the magnetic declination.

q: 42. Azimuth (direct angles) is an angle measured in
explain: Azimuth is measured clockwise from the North (or South) meridian.

q: 43. The true or geographical meridians through the various stations
options: converge from north pole to south pole
converge from south pole to north pole
explain: Unlike grid lines (which are parallel), true geographical meridians through different stations are not parallel; they converge toward the north and south poles.

q: 44. The line in which the plane passing through the given point and the north and south poles intersects the surface of the earth is called
explain: This is the definition of the true (geographical) meridian at a point - the line formed by the intersection of the earth's surface with the plane through that point and both geographic poles.

q: 45. The smaller horizontal angle between the true meridian and a survey line, is known
explain: The smaller horizontal angle (within 90 degrees) between the true meridian and a survey line, expressed with quadrant letters, is known as the reduced bearing of the line.

q: 46. If the whole circle bearing of a line is 120, its quadrant bearing is
explain: For a WCB of 120 degrees (in the second quadrant, between 90 and 180), the reduced (quadrant) bearing is measured from south: 180-120 = S60 E.

q: 47. If the whole circle bearing of a line is 270 its reduced bearing is
explain: Note: standard convention for a WCB of 270 degrees (due west) gives a reduced bearing of N90W; the printed answer key here shows S90W, which appears to be a possible misprint - please verify against your copy.

q: 48. If the whole circle bearing of a line is 180, its reduced bearing is
explain: A WCB of exactly 180 degrees corresponds to due south, so its reduced bearing is simply expressed as S (south).

q: 49. Diurnal variation of magnetic declination is
options: greater at equator than nearer the poles
less at equator than nearer the poles
less in summer than nearer the poles
same at all latitudes and during different months
explain: Diurnal (daily) variation of magnetic declination is generally observed to be greater near the magnetic equator compared to regions nearer the poles.

q: 50. Isogonic lines are the lines having the same
explain: Isogonic lines connect points on a map having equal magnetic declination at a given time.

q: 51. If whole circle bearing of a line is 120, its reduced bearing is
explain: For a WCB of 120 degrees (second quadrant), the reduced bearing is measured from south: 180-120 = S60 E.

q: 52. The magnetic bearing of a lines is 55 30' and the magnetic declination is 4 30' west. The true bearing of a line will be
explain: For a westerly declination, true bearing = magnetic bearing - declination: 55 30' - 4 30' = 51 degrees.
